ai.title: Terminal watchdog test suite restructured with platform-specific
ai.summary: Refactored terminal-watchdog.test.ts to spawn all fixtures in a single beforeAll hook with shared platform-aware timeouts (60s Windows, 15s Unix for ready state) instead of per-test spawns. Fixture arm deadline extended to 40s to prevent false negatives on slow runners. Diagnostics now include exact marker paths and timing budgets in error output.

eli5.text: The automated checker that makes sure the terminal watchdog works correctly has been reorganized so all the test pieces start up at the same time in one shared setup step, rather than each test starting its own piece individually. This is only a test-suite change, meaning nothing in the actual product is different, it affects the internal quality checks, not what you see when you use it. If you looked at the test results, you might notice the overall test run is more reliable on slower computers, especially Windows machines, because the built-in timer for waiting on everything to get ready was given more room to complete.

ai.title: Shared CLI auth code lifetime constant
ai.summary: Added `common/src/constants/auth.ts` exporting `CLI_AUTH_CODE_LIFETIME_MS` (1 hour). Unifies device-code expiration logic across CLI (codebuff.com) and Desktop (freebuff.com) surfaces. Prevents drift where one app times out earlier than the other due to hardcoded values. Clients use `expiresInMs` from API responses to avoid clock-skew bugs when validating `expiresAt`.

eli5.text: The sign-in code you get when logging in on a new device now expires after exactly one hour, the same for both the command-line tool and the desktop app. Previously each app tracked that timer separately, so one could expire sooner than the other without any obvious reason. You would not see a new setting or button; the change just keeps both apps from disagreeing about when a code stops working. Because this constant is now shared and used by the response the server sends back, the moment it takes effect is whenever the server you connect to runs this updated code.

facts: Split out of `ancillary`, because one shared budget wide enough for account_providers (75ms p50 on 2 round trips) was blind to lanes that actually run at 2-6ms. A budget that every lane passes is not a budget.

Still REPORTED, never paged, see the `breach` comment in evaluateDatabaseRequestCosts. Promoting these to pageable is a deliberate follow-up, and the precondition is a full week with every lane inside them.
The lane most worth driving down is `session_post`: 19 round trips at p95. With transport at ~11ms that is ~210ms of pure round-tripping, and round trips, not query time, are what handlers control.
One indexed read, on both services. The tightest lane we have, and the clearest read on transport cost: 1 round trip, so its p50 IS the floor.

The absolute budgets used to be unpageable for a hard reason: they were written against server execution time while this metric measures CLIENT wall time, so every lane sat 4-25x over them and paging made this alert red on every run for days, the same as no alert. That reason is gone.

ai.title: Recalibrate database request cost budgets to measured production
ai.summary: Updated `DATABASE_REQUEST_BUDGETS` in `common/src/util/database-request-cost.ts` to reflect post-private-endpoint traffic (~11.8ms/round-trip) rather than aspirational server-execution targets. Split `ancillary` into `light` and `ancillary` lanes to expose fast paths (e.g., `streak_get`, `cli_auth_status`) previously masked by wide budgets. Budgets now serve as a no-regression ratchet; absolute breaches remain reported-only until a full week of clean data validates them for paging.

eli5.text: The system that tracks how long database lookups take has been recalibrated to match real-world performance after a network change made those lookups about 10x faster. The old limits were based on how fast the database should theoretically be, so every lookup blew past them constantly and nobody paid attention. Now the limits are set just above what actually happens, split into finer groups so a fast lookup (like checking if you're logged in) isn't hidden behind a slow one. Breaches still don't send alerts yet, the team needs a full week of everything staying under the new limits first, so this just quietly starts collecting data today.

facts: Bytes of the binary's stderr kept for the crash report.
A startup death that is probably this machine failing to run the optimized build, reported under the *other* Windows spelling.
Everything else: strip the control bytes and keep the text. An OSC or a lone escape loses its introducer and degrades to inert characters, which is all a crash report needs it to be.
Reached only once the baseline fallback has declined or failed, so name the case the user can still act on instead of leaving them with an abort code and a bug-tracker link.
Watch a launch so its death can be explained: how long the binary lived, and what it printed on the way out.

ai.title: Launcher detects Windows startup abort as CPU-feature suspect
ai.summary: The launcher now distinguishes a confirmed illegal-instruction exit from a Windows startup abort reported as NTSTATUS 0xC0000409, which is the *other* spelling Bun's Zig panic uses for a missing AVX2 instruction set. A new `isStartupCpuFeatureCrash(code, signal, msAlive)` check bounds that suspicion to the first `STARTUP_CRASH_WINDOW_MS` (10000) milliseconds of life, so a panic ten minutes into a session is no longer misread as a CPU lacking AVX2. `watchLaunch` times each child and tees the last `STDERR_TAIL_BYTES` (8192) of its stderr through `sanitizeForReplay`, which strips terminal-rewriting escapes so the captured panic text can be printed back after `resetTerminal`. `tryFallbackToBaseline` only persists the no-AVX2 verdict for a confirmed `SIGILL`/`0xc000001d`, leaving suspected crashes to ride the slower baseline build without writing a CPU limitation into `cpu-features.json`.
ai.evidence: In `cli/release-core/launcher.js`, new constants `STARTUP_CRASH_WINDOW_MS = 10000` and `STDERR_TAIL_BYTES = 8192` are defined, `isStartupCpuFeatureCrash(code, signal, msAlive)` detects a Windows startup abort (0xC0000409) within that window, `tryFallbackToBaseline` now accepts `msAlive` and distinguishes a confirmed illegal instruction from a suspected startup CPU-feature abort, `watchLaunch(child)` is attached to every spawned child to time-to-live and tee the last 8192 bytes of its stderr, and `printCrashDiagnostics` now prints a sanitized stderr tail and branches on `msAlive`.
ai.migration: No action is required from users; the baseline fallback is triggered automatically when a Windows startup abort matches the new `isStartupCpuFeatureCrash` heuristic.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show who consumes the new `__testing` exports `isStartupCpuFeatureCrash` and `tryFallbackToBaseline` or when the windows startup-abort detection tests will be wired into CI.

facts: RATIO AND FLOORS ARE SET FROM MEASURED NOISE, not intuition, both were too tight and the alert paged on ordinary traffic within a day of shipping.

No ratio separates a 2.3x-noisy p50 from a real 2x regression, and 4-6x on p50RoundTrips is hopeless. Both produced false pages on 2026-08-10 ("roundTrips.p50 regressed 2 -> 5"; session_post's p50 wall moving 9ms -> 20ms). Still reported via the budgets, just not pageable.

ai.title: Database cost regression thresholds recalibrated to silence false
ai.summary:
The default regression thresholds in `common/src/util/database-request-cost.ts` were tightened after the August 10 alert paged on ordinary diurnal traffic: `regressionRatio` rose from 1.5 to 2.0, `minClientSqlWallRegressionMs` rose from 20 to 150, and `minRoundTripRegression` rose from 2 to 8. A new `REGRESSION_FLOOR_BUDGET_SHARE = 0.375` constant scales the absolute floor down per lane using the lane's own budget, so light lanes like `cli_auth_status` (p95 10-15ms) still get a proportionate, pageable floor rather than being blind to a 10x regression.

The change leaves the reporting-only over-budget lane in place and does not promote it to a pageable signal; the commit comment keeps absolute budgets reported only and states they are promoted only after a week clean, following the noise table measured from nine post-private-endpoint hours. The `breach` flag continues to gate paging on `regressed.length > 0`, now excluding p50 entirely so the typical-request percentile can no longer fire a page.
ai.evidence: The diff modifies `common/src/util/database-request-cost.ts`, raising `regressionRatio` from 1.5 to 2.0, `minClientSqlWallRegressionMs` from 20 to 150, and `minRoundTripRegression` from 2 to 8 in `DEFAULT_DATABASE_COST_EVALUATION_OPTIONS`, and adding the `REGRESSION_FLOOR_BUDGET_SHARE = 0.375` constant used in `evaluateFamily` to scale the absolute floor down for light lanes via `Math.min(minRegression, limit * REGRESSION_FLOOR_BUDGET_SHARE)`.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not identify who consumes the recalibrated thresholds outside `evaluateDatabaseRequestCosts` or confirm when a week of clean over-budget traffic triggers promotion to a pageable signal. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

ai.title: Drop knowledge.md from knowledge file priority, default /init
ai.summary: The `PRIMARY_KNOWLEDGE_FILE_NAME` constant has been removed from `common/src/constants/knowledge.ts`, and `knowledge.md` has been dropped from the `KNOWLEDGE_FILE_NAMES` array so the priority order is now `AGENTS.md` then `CLAUDE.md`. As a result, `/init` in `cli/src/commands/init.ts` now scaffolds `AGENTS.md` (via `KNOWLEDGE_FILE_NAMES[0]`) instead of `knowledge.md`, and the agent runtime in `packages/agent-runtime/src/templates/strings.ts` injects only root-level priority knowledge files into the `PLACEHOLDER.KNOWLEDGE_FILES_CONTENTS` slot, wrapped in a labeled `Project instructions:` block when present. The SDK re-exports in `sdk/src/run-state.ts` were updated to drop the removed symbol, and `agents/base3.ts` now includes the knowledge-files placeholder in its system prompt. This realigns the knowledge-file priority used for both project scaffolding and runtime injection.
ai.evidence: Removed `PRIMARY_KNOWLEDGE_FILE_NAME` from `common/src/constants/knowledge.ts`, dropping `'knowledge.md'` from the `KNOWLEDGE_FILE_NAMES` array and updating JSDoc that previously ranked `knowledge.md` highest; `cli/src/commands/init.ts` now imports `KNOWLEDGE_FILE_NAMES` and uses `KNOWLEDGE_FILE_NAMES[0]` (which is now `'AGENTS.md'`) in place of the removed constant for path construction and tracking; `packages/agent-runtime/src/templates/strings.ts` filters injected knowledge blocks to `KNOWLEDGE_FILE_NAMES_LOWERCASE` and restructures the injection to emit a labeled `Project instructions:` block only when blocks exist; `sdk/src/run-state.ts` re-exports the new list and removes the re-export of `PRIMARY_KNOWLEDGE_FILE_NAME`, with priority comments updated to `AGENTS.md > CLAUDE.md`; `agents/base3.ts` adds `${PLACEHOLDER.KNOWLEDGE_FILES_CONTENTS}` into the system prompt and relies on the new knowledge-file priority at injection time.
ai.migration: If your project relied on `/init` creating `knowledge.md` or on `knowledge.md` being the injected knowledge file, you must rename it to `AGENTS.md` so it is picked up by the new priority list.
ai.unknowns: The change does not show whether existing `knowledge.md` files are migrated automatically or simply stop being recognized as knowledge files.

ai.title: Pin Muse Spark reasoning effort to high
ai.summary: Added FREEBUFF_MUSE_SPARK_REASONING_EFFORT constant set to 'high' and wired it to MUSE_SPARK_12_CONTRIBUTOR_MODEL. Updated getFreebuffModelReasoningEffort to check FREEBUFF_WEB_ALL_MODELS as a fallback alongside SUPPORTED_FREEBUFF_MODELS. This ensures Web-only models like Muse Spark correctly resolve their reasoning effort, which previously failed due to the CLI/Desktop catalog exclusion.

eli5.text: You are now guaranteed to get the same, high-quality reasoning from Muse Spark every time you use it, instead of that behaviour being left to chance. Previously, the system had decided how deeply the model should think on your request, but a lookup glitch meant that decision could silently fall away for web-based users. The developers pinned that reasoning depth to 'high' explicitly and fixed the lookup so it now checks the full catalog of available models, ensuring the setting actually reaches every Muse Spark request you make.

entries.summary: Shared/Core changes across 1 file(s) (+29/−14).

ai.title: Muse Spark reasoning effort set to xhigh, enum widened to provider
ai.summary: FREEBUFF_MUSE_SPARK_REASONING_EFFORT in common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts switches from high to xhigh, and the FreebuffModelOption.reasoningEffort type widens from low/medium/high to minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh to match Meta's provider scale. The change reflects live measurements on Muse Spark: xhigh buys ~8% more reasoning tokens than high at ~26% higher latency, while minimal cuts reasoning 2.4x with no observed accuracy loss on tested samples. The wider enum lives on the model row rather than agent-definition.ts so one provider's extra rung does not leak into values every published agent can declare. Scope is shared core constants only; no CLI picker, Web/Desktop, or docs files carry the change.

eli5.text: If you send a question to the Muse Spark helper, it will now spend more time thinking before it answers. The extra thinking time is modest, roughly a quarter again longer to wait for a reply, and it only adds about 8% more internal reasoning, so most turns will feel slightly slower with a little more careful digging behind the scenes. The team also opened up the setting that controls how deeply any given model is allowed to think, so one model's extra level of effort doesn't force that same extra level onto every other model. These adjustments are live today in the core system that routes requests; nothing on your screen changes, just how much silent work happens before a reply shows up.
